chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed li'an with his wife while she was pregnant, then he claimed her child after she gave birth, alleging that it was from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The child is returned to him, and he is not whipped, because the li'an has passed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child if the father performs li'an with his pregnant wife and later claims paternity?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a husband who performs li'an with his pregnant wife and subsequently claims paternity of the born child is returned the child and exempt from the li'an penalty of whipping, as the ceremony is considered complete. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the finality of the li'an process precludes the application of the hadd punishment for slander, even if the husband later asserts ownership of the offspring. The case underscores the procedural closure of the li'an mechanism in resolving lineage disputes.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who cursed his wife, and she was pregnant. Then he called her child, after it had been born, and alleged that it was from him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The child would be return to him, and he would not be whipped because the cursing has passed’.
